metadata.name: WordPress Core Execution Tests - Hooks
metadata.description: Code generation tasks for WordPress Hooks APIs

tests.prompt: Implement a function that attaches a filter to the_title that appends the literal suffix ' [WPBP]' to the incoming title string.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_hooks_001()` registers a `the_title` filter whose callback returns the original title plus ` [WPBP]`. Runtime validation calls the function and applies the WordPress title filter to sample values to verify the appended result.
requirements: Use add_filter() on the the_title filter
Append the suffix without replacing the original title

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_hooks_001' ) ) { return false; } wpbp_hooks_001(); return 'Hello [WPBP]' === apply_filters( 'the_title', 'Hello', 123 ) && 'Draft [WPBP]' === apply_filters( 'the_title', 'Draft', 456 );
assertions.description: The title filter appends the required suffix to filtered titles

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_hooks_001(): void { add_filter( 'the_title', function ( $title ) { return $title . ' [WPBP]'; }, 10, 1 ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that registers an action on wpbp_two_args. When the action fires with two arguments, store them as '<first>:<second>' in the option wpbp_two_args_result.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_hooks_002()` registers an action callback for `wpbp_two_args` that accepts both action arguments and writes them to `wpbp_two_args_result` in order. Runtime validation fires the action with two values and reads the option written by the callback.
requirements: Use add_action() with two accepted arguments
Preserve both action arguments in order

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_hooks_002' ) ) { return false; } wpbp_hooks_002(); do_action( 'wpbp_two_args', 'alpha', 'beta' ); return 'alpha:beta' === get_option( 'wpbp_two_args_result' );
assertions.description: The action callback receives both arguments and stores them in order

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_hooks_002(): void { add_action( 'wpbp_two_args', function ( $a, $b ) { update_option( 'wpbp_two_args_result', $a . ':' . $b ); }, 10, 2 ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that removes a supplied callback from the wpbp_remove_filter hook at priority 0 and returns true only when WordPress reports it was present before removal and absent afterward.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_hooks_003()` checks a supplied callback with `has_filter()`, removes it from `wpbp_remove_filter` at priority 0 with `remove_filter()`, and treats priority 0 as a valid registration rather than a falsey miss. Runtime validation pre-registers a callback at priority 0 and verifies the filter no longer changes a value.
requirements: Use has_filter() to inspect the callback registration
Use remove_filter() with the matching priority
Treat priority 0 as a valid registered priority

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_hooks_003' ) ) { return false; } $callback = $GLOBALS['wpbp_hooks_003_callback'] ?? null; if ( ! is_callable( $callback ) ) { return false; } $ok = wpbp_hooks_003( $callback ); return true === $ok && false === has_filter( 'wpbp_remove_filter', $callback ) && 'seed' === apply_filters( 'wpbp_remove_filter', 'seed' );
assertions.description: The priority-0 callback is removed and no longer affects filtered values

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_hooks_003( callable $callback ): bool { $before = has_filter( 'wpbp_remove_filter', $callback ); $removed = remove_filter( 'wpbp_remove_filter', $callback, 0 ); $after = has_filter( 'wpbp_remove_filter', $callback ); return 0 === $before && true === $removed && false === $after; }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that registers two callbacks on wpbp_priority: a lower-priority callback appends 'A' and a later callback appends 'B', then returns the filtered value starting from an empty string.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_hooks_004()` uses `add_filter()` priorities on `wpbp_priority` and returns the result of `apply_filters()`. Runtime validation expects WordPress to run the lower numeric priority first so the final value is `AB`.
requirements: Use apply_filters() to return the computed value

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_hooks_004' ) ) { return false; } return 'AB' === wpbp_hooks_004();
assertions.description: Filter callbacks run in WordPress priority order

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_hooks_004(): string { add_filter( 'wpbp_priority', fn( $v ) => $v . 'B', 20 ); add_filter( 'wpbp_priority', fn( $v ) => $v . 'A', 5 ); return apply_filters( 'wpbp_priority', '' ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that fires the custom action wpbp_did_action twice and returns WordPress's count for that action.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_hooks_005()` dispatches `wpbp_did_action` twice with `do_action()` and returns `did_action( 'wpbp_did_action' )`. Runtime validation checks the returned count and WordPress's recorded action count.
requirements: Use do_action() to fire the action
Use did_action() to return the action count

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_hooks_005' ) ) { return false; } return 2 === wpbp_hooks_005() && 2 === did_action( 'wpbp_did_action' );
assertions.description: did_action() reports the exact number of dispatched actions

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_hooks_005(): int { do_action( 'wpbp_did_action' ); do_action( 'wpbp_did_action' ); return did_action( 'wpbp_did_action' ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that removes every callback from the wpbp_remove_all filter and returns true when applying that filter to 'abc' leaves it unchanged.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_hooks_006()` calls `remove_all_filters()` for `wpbp_remove_all` and verifies through `apply_filters()` that callbacks on that hook no longer alter the value. Runtime validation pre-registers callbacks before the submitted code runs and confirms the hook is empty afterward.
requirements: Use remove_all_filters() on the custom filter
Use apply_filters() to verify the value is no longer changed

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_hooks_006' ) ) { return false; } return true === wpbp_hooks_006() && false === has_filter( 'wpbp_remove_all' ) && 'abc' === apply_filters( 'wpbp_remove_all', 'abc' );
assertions.description: All callbacks are removed from the filter hook

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_hooks_006(): bool { remove_all_filters( 'wpbp_remove_all' ); return 'abc' === apply_filters( 'wpbp_remove_all', 'abc' ); }

tests.prompt: Late-loading integrations often attach to an action that has already run, and their callback then never fires. Implement a function that attaches a callback to an action, except that when the action has already fired at least once it invokes the callback immediately instead of registering it. Return 'ran' when it invoked the callback and 'deferred' when it registered it for later.
tests.expected_behavior: The decision has to come from `did_action( $hook )`, which counts how many times the action has fired; `has_action()` or a static flag cannot tell. Runtime validation fires one action before the submitted code runs, then checks the already-fired hook invokes the callback once and leaves no registration behind, while the not-yet-fired hook registers the callback and runs it when the action is later fired.
requirements: Invoke the callback immediately, exactly once, when the action has already fired
Register the callback on the action when it has not fired yet, so it runs when the action fires
Return 'ran' for the immediate case and 'deferred' for the registered case

required_patterns.description: Checks whether the action already fired
Registers the callback for the not-yet-fired case
Invokes the callback for the already-fired case

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_hooks_007' ) ) { return false; } $callback = $GLOBALS['wpbp_hooks_007_callback'] ?? null; if ( ! is_callable( $callback ) ) { return false; } $GLOBALS['wpbp_hooks_007_count'] = 0; if ( 'ran' !== wpbp_hooks_007( 'wpbp_boot_done', $callback ) ) { return false; } if ( 1 !== $GLOBALS['wpbp_hooks_007_count'] ) { return false; } if ( false !== has_action( 'wpbp_boot_done', $callback ) ) { return false; } if ( 'deferred' !== wpbp_hooks_007( 'wpbp_later_step', $callback ) ) { return false; } if ( 1 !== $GLOBALS['wpbp_hooks_007_count'] ) { return false; } if ( false === has_action( 'wpbp_later_step', $callback ) ) { return false; } do_action( 'wpbp_later_step' ); return 2 === $GLOBALS['wpbp_hooks_007_count'];
assertions.description: An already-fired action runs the callback once immediately, a pending action defers it until the action fires

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_hooks_007( string $hook, callable $callback ): string { if ( did_action( $hook ) > 0 ) { call_user_func( $callback ); return 'ran'; } add_action( $hook, $callback ); return 'deferred'; }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_hooks_007( string $hook, callable $callback ): string { add_action( $hook, $callback ); return 'deferred'; }
function wpbp_hooks_007( string $hook, callable $callback ): string { if ( has_action( $hook ) ) { call_user_func( $callback ); return 'ran'; } add_action( $hook, $callback ); return 'deferred'; }
function wpbp_hooks_007( string $hook, callable $callback ): string { call_user_func( $callback ); return 'ran'; }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that moves a callback that is already attached to a filter to a different priority on that same hook, so it still runs exactly once but in its new position. Return the priority the callback was previously attached at, or false when the callback is not attached to that hook at all. A callback attached at priority 0 is attached.
tests.expected_behavior: `has_filter()` returns the integer priority when the callback is attached and `false` when it is not, so a truthiness test misreads priority 0, and `remove_filter()` only removes a callback when it is given the priority the callback is actually registered at — passing the new priority leaves the old registration in place and the callback then runs twice. Runtime validation registers a callback at priority 0 ahead of one at priority 10, moves the first to 20, and checks the returned priority, the new registration and the resulting filter output, then repeats with a callback that was never attached.
requirements: Return the previous priority as an integer, treating priority 0 as attached
Return false, and change nothing, when the callback is not attached to the hook
After the move the callback must be attached only at the new priority

required_patterns.description: Registers the callback at the new priority

runtime_checks.setup: $GLOBALS['wpbp_hooks_008'] = array( 'a' => static function ( $value ) { return $value . 'A'; }, 'b' => static function ( $value ) { return $value . 'B'; }, 'c' => static function ( $value ) { return $value . 'C'; } ); add_filter( 'wpbp_move_priority', $GLOBALS['wpbp_hooks_008']['a'], 0 ); add_filter( 'wpbp_move_priority', $GLOBALS['wpbp_hooks_008']['b'], 10 );

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_hooks_008' ) ) { return false; } $callbacks = (array) ( $GLOBALS['wpbp_hooks_008'] ?? array() ); if ( 3 !== count( $callbacks ) ) { return false; } if ( 'AB' !== apply_filters( 'wpbp_move_priority', '' ) ) { return false; } $previous = wpbp_hooks_008( 'wpbp_move_priority', $callbacks['a'], 20 ); if ( 0 !== $previous ) { return false; } if ( 20 !== has_filter( 'wpbp_move_priority', $callbacks['a'] ) ) { return false; } if ( 'BA' !== apply_filters( 'wpbp_move_priority', '' ) ) { return false; } $missing = wpbp_hooks_008( 'wpbp_move_priority', $callbacks['c'], 20 ); if ( false !== $missing ) { return false; } if ( false !== has_filter( 'wpbp_move_priority', $callbacks['c'] ) ) { return false; } return 'BA' === apply_filters( 'wpbp_move_priority', '' );
assertions.description: A priority 0 callback reports 0 and moves to the new position once, and an unattached callback reports false

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_hooks_008( string $hook, callable $callback, int $new_priority ) { $current = has_filter( $hook, $callback ); if ( false === $current ) { return false; } $current = (int) $current; remove_filter( $hook, $callback, $current ); add_filter( $hook, $callback, $new_priority ); return $current; }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_hooks_008( string $hook, callable $callback, int $new_priority ) { $current = has_filter( $hook, $callback ); if ( ! $current ) { return false; } remove_filter( $hook, $callback, (int) $current ); add_filter( $hook, $callback, $new_priority ); return (int) $current; }

function wpbp_hooks_008( string $hook, callable $callback, int $new_priority ) { $current = has_filter( $hook, $callback ); if ( false === $current ) { return false; } remove_filter( $hook, $callback, $new_priority ); add_filter( $hook, $callback, $new_priority ); return (int) $current; }
